Put $p_i = \sum_{j < i} m_j d_j$, and let the basic dimension list be the concatenation, for $i = 0, \dots, k - 1$ in order, of $\sum_{j=0}^{m_i - 1} q^{p_i + j d_i}$ copies of $d_i$. nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number and $(d_0, m_0), \dots, (d_{k-1}, m_{k-1})$ a list of blocks, and put $p_i = \sum_{j < i} m_j d_j$. The basic multiplicity of block $i$ is $N_i = \sum_{j=0}^{m_i - 1} q^{p_i + j d_i}$ when $i < k$, and $N_i = 0$ when $i \ge k$.

The final dimension list of block $i$ is defined when $C$ has an entry $s_1, \dots, s_r$ at index $i$: start from $N_i$ copies of $d_i$, where $N_i$ is the basic multiplicity of block $i$ (the empty list when $i \ge k$), and for $t = 1, \dots, r$ in order apply the split replacement of…
nodes.title: Final dimensions of a block

nodes.summary: A block is a pair $(d, m)$ of natural numbers, read as a part size $d$ of an integer partition together with its multiplicity $m$. No condition is imposed on a single block.
nodes.title: Block

nodes.summary: Let $(d_0, m_0), \dots, (d_{k-1}, m_{k-1})$ be a list of blocks and put $p_i = \sum_{j < i} m_j d_j$. The first-split exponent of block $i$ is $u_i = p_i + (m_i - 1) d_i$ when $i < k$, where $m_i - 1$ is taken to be $0$ if $m_i = 0$, and $u_i = 0$ when $i \ge k$.
nodes.title: First-split exponent

nodes.summary: A branch step is a triple $(a, b, c)$ of natural numbers. It describes one simultaneous split level: for the ambient parameter $q$, $c$ copies of the parent dimension $a + b$ become $c$ copies of $a$ and $c q^a$ copies of $b$.
nodes.title: Branch step

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number, $(d_0, m_0), \dots, (d_{k-1}, m_{k-1})$ a list of blocks and $i$ an index, and let $u_i$ and $N_i$ be the first-split exponent and the basic multiplicity of block $i$, with $d_i$ read as $0$ when $i \ge k$. A chain of branch steps $(a_1, b_1, c_1), \dots, (a_r, b_r, c_r)$ is a valid branch for block $i$ when either $r = 0$, or $r \ge 1$, the first step satisfies $1 \le b_1 \le a_1$,…
nodes.title: Valid branch

nodes.summary: A chain of branch steps $(a_1, b_1, c_1), \dots, (a_r, b_r, c_r)$ is adjacently valid when for every $j$ with $1 \le j < r$ we have $a_{j+1} + b_{j+1} = a_j$, $1 \le b_{j+1} \le a_{j+1}$ and $1 \le c_{j+1} \le c_j$. Only consecutive steps are related, and nothing is required of the first step alone; in particular every chain with at most one step is adjacently valid.

nodes.summary: A Gaussian partition is represented by its list of subspace dimensions, which is a nonincreasing list of natural numbers.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
